# SOP-P2-L3-04 Shift handover - Machining line
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, EQ-P2-L3-IH03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-037, SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02

Purpose
1. Document the required actions for a consistent, auditable shift handover on Machining line P2-L3. This SOP defines the preconditions, information transfer, verification steps, and sign-off required to maintain continuity of safe, quality production.

Background and rationale
2. Handover is a critical control point to prevent production loss, quality escapes, and safety incidents. Consistent transfer of machine state, tooling, process parameters, consumable status, and outstanding actions minimizes risk during shift changes and supports traceability for investigations and continuous improvement. This SOP aligns with requirements in ECN-2026-037 and references operational details in SOP-P2-L3-01 and SOP-P2-L3-02.

Preconditions (what must be true before the handover begins)
3. Outgoing operator must be at the machine control desk or authorized location; incoming operator must have valid line access credentials and training per SOP-P2-L3-01.  
4. All completed production lots for the shift must have been entered into the MES and any nonconforming product tagged per SOP-P2-L3-02.  
5. Equipment status must be confirmed as available or isolated per lockout/tagout rules before any hands-on work; if equipment is isolated, reference ECN-2026-037 for change control.

Required PPE
6. Minimum PPE for the handover walkthrough: safety glasses, steel-toe boots, hearing protection, and cut-resistant gloves when handling tooling or parts. Operators must also wear high-visibility vests. If maintenance activity is in progress, add arc-rated clothing and face shield as required by the maintenance permit.

Key records to prepare and retain
7. Handover log entry in the shift register (electronic or paper) with: outgoing operator name, incoming operator name, start and end time of handover, a concise list of open issues, and signatures. Retain the handover log as per document retention rules.  
8. Copies or links to any pending work orders, nonconformance reports, maintenance requests, or quality hold tags referenced during the handover. Store these with the shift log for audit.

Step-by-step handover procedure
9. Step 1 — Pre-handover briefing at machine: Outgoing operator summarizes the shift outcome, including completed lots, in-process lot IDs, and any deviations. Include status of EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and EQ-P2-L3-IH03 and note any abnormal alarms or recent resets. Example: if a surface finish issue was observed, state where affected parts are staged and the containment action taken. Rationale: verbal transfer ensures complex issues are highlighted.

10. Step 2 — Visual and written status check: Walk the production flow with incoming operator. Verify machine guards, coolant levels, tooling condition, chip accumulation, and housekeeping. Record any deficiencies in the shift register. Rationale: physical confirmation prevents reliance on memory.

11. Step 3 — Consumables and lubricant check: Confirm quantities and part numbers on site. The lubricant part number for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is CFW-LUB-225. The lubricant part number for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is CFW-LUB-725. If lubricant is below the operational minimum on-site, initiate a replenishment request per SOP-P2-L3-02 and note the action in the log. Rationale: using the correct lubricant part maintains equipment performance and prevents warranty or metallurgical issues.

12. Step 4 — Process parameter and setup verification: Outgoing operator shows incoming operator the current program, offsets, and tool list. Incoming operator confirms they can access the same program and understands any offsets applied. If adjustments were made during the shift, document the reason and the exact change in the shift register and reference the related work order. Rationale: prevents accidental program mismatch.

13. Step 5 — Outstanding issues and containment: Review open nonconformances, machine faults, and in-progress maintenance tasks. For each item, state the status, responsible person, and next action. Example record entry: "Tool holder replacement required, work order created, awaiting parts." Rationale: assigns clear responsibility and prevents dropped tasks.

14. Step 6 — Safety and quality checks: Confirm emergency stops, e-stops, and safety interlocks are functional; verify the location of first aid kit and fire extinguisher for the incoming operator. Confirm that the quality inspection point for in-process checks is staffed or scheduled. Rationale: immediate access to safety equipment is essential and inspection continuity prevents quality escapes.

15. Step 7 — Documentation and MES updates: Outgoing operator updates MES with final cycle counts, rejects, downtime reasons, and any job changes. Incoming operator verifies the MES reflects the same status before taking control. Rationale: single source of truth for production data.

16. Step 8 — Final verbal acknowledgement and sign-off: Both operators read back any critical actions or deviations. The incoming operator confirms acceptance and assumes responsibility by signing the shift register. Record time of handover completion. Rationale: readback reduces misunderstandings.

Examples of acceptable handover entries
17. Example 1: "Shift: B, Outgoing: J. Smith, Incoming: A. Perez. EQ-P2-L3-RR01 operating, CFW-LUB-225 on-site x2 drums, no leaks. In-process lot ID 4123 at op 3. Nonconformance NC-78 staged. MES updated. Handover complete."  
18. Example 2: "Shift: C, Outgoing: L. Chen, Incoming: M. Patel. EQ-P2-L3-IH03 preheat stable, lubricant CFW-LUB-725 low, replenishment requested WO-908. Quality hold on lot 4150. Handover complete."

Records to keep and retention
19. Keep the signed handover log and associated electronic MES snapshot for each shift. Attach any related nonconformance records or maintenance requests. Retain files per the company retention schedule and reference ECN-2026-037 for archival requirements.

Deviations and escalation
20. If the incoming operator does not agree with the outgoing status on any critical item, do not accept the handover. Escalate to the line supervisor and document the disagreement in the log. If the disagreement involves equipment safety, place the equipment in a safe state and isolate as required.

Training and competency
21. Operators must demonstrate handover competence during training per SOP-P2-L3-01. Supervisors will audit handovers periodically and document results.

Sign-off
22. Outgoing operator name and signature: ____________________  
23. Incoming operator name and signature: ____________________  
24. Supervisor name and signature (if required): ____________________

References
25. ECN-2026-037  
26. SOP-P2-L3-01  
27. SOP-P2-L3-02
